title: 1959 AHSME Problem 3
statement: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral are perpendicular to each other, the figure would always be included under the general classification:

solutions.text:
A kite can have perpendicular diagonals without being a rhombus, rectangle, square, or isosceles trapezoid. Therefore perpendicular diagonals alone do not force any of the first four classifications.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Look for a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals that is not one of the four named special types
A general kite supplies a useful counterexample
